'''Erich Leo Lehmann''' (20 November 1917 – 12 September 2009) was a German-born American [[statistician]], who made a major contribution to [[nonparametric]] [[hypothesis testing]].<ref name="chronicle">{{cite news
 |title=Erich L. Lehmann – Berkeley professor – dies
 |newspaper=San Francisco Chronicle
 |author=Nanette Asimov
 |date=October 16, 2009
 |url=http://www.sfgate.com/cgi-bin/article.cgi?f=/c/a/2009/10/15/BAJP1A535I.DTL&type=science
 |archive-url=https://archive.today/20121210041739/http://www.sfgate.com/cgi-bin/article.cgi?f=/c/a/2009/10/15/BAJP1A535I.DTL&type=science
 |url-status=dead
 |archive-date=December 10, 2012
 |access-date=2009-12-12
}}</ref> He is one of the [[eponym]]s of the [[Lehmann–Scheffé theorem]] and of the [[Hodges–Lehmann estimator]].

==Early life==
Lehmann was born in [[Strasbourg]], [[Alsace-Lorraine]] in 1917 to a family of [[Ashkenazi Jewish]] ancestry. He grew up in [[Frankfurt am Main]], Germany, until the [[Machtergreifung]] in 1933, when his family fled to [[Switzerland]] to escape the [[Nazi]]s.<ref name="chronicle" /> He graduated from high school in Zurich, and studied mathematics for two years at [[Trinity College, Cambridge]]. Following that, he emigrated to the United States, arriving in New York in late 1940. He enrolled in [[University of California, Berkeley]] as a post-graduate student—albeit without a prior degree—in 1941.<ref name="rojo">
{{cite journal
 |last=Rojo|first=E.L.
 |title=Erich Leo Lehmann—A Glimpse into his Life and Work
 |journal= [[The Annals of Statistics]]
 |volume=39 |issue=5 |year=2011 |pages=2244–2265
 |doi=10.1214/11-AOS927
|arxiv=1202.5096|s2cid=88512438
 }}</ref>

==Career==
Lehmann obtained his [[Master of Arts|MA]] in mathematics in 1942 and his [[PhD]] (under [[Jerzy Neyman]]) in 1946, at the [[University of California, Berkeley]], where he taught from 1942.<ref name="rojo"/> From August 1944 to August 1945 he worked as an operations analyst for the [[United States Air Force]] on [[Guam]].<ref name="rojo"/>  He taught at [[Columbia University]] and at [[Princeton University]] during 1950–51, and then during 1951–1952 he was a visiting associate professor at [[Stanford University]].

He was an editor of the ''[[Annals of Mathematical Statistics]]'' and president of the [[Institute of Mathematical Statistics]], and a member of the [[American Academy of Arts and Sciences]] and the [[National Academy of Sciences]].

In 1977 he married another statistician, [[Juliet Popper Shaffer]], whom he had met four years earlier as the sponsor to her sabbatical visit to Berkeley. In the same year, Shaffer moved from being a psychology professor at the [[University of Kansas]] to a lecturer position in statistics at Berkeley.<ref>{{citation
 | last = Lehmann | first = E. L. | title = Reminiscences of a Statistician | chapter = New Tasks and Relationships | author-link = Erich Leo Lehmann
 | doi = 10.1007/978-0-387-71597-1_13
 | isbn = 978-0-387-71596-4
 | location = New York
 | mr = 2367933
 | pages = 212–216
 | publisher = Springer
 | year = 2008}}</ref>

In 1997, on the occasion of his eightieth birthday, the department of statistics at the [[University of California at Berkeley]] created the Erich Lehmann Fund in Statistics<ref>[http://statistics.berkeley.edu/erich-lehmann-fund-statistics Erich Lehmann Fund in Statistics]</ref> to support the students of the department.
